## Cause
`QuerySet._check_bulk_create_options()` (`django/db/models/query.py`) converted `update_fields`/`unique_fields` from names to **Field objects**, but `SQLInsertCompiler.as_sql()` (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py`) then passed `self.query.update_fields`/`unique_fields` straight into `connection.ops.on_conflict_suffix_sql()`, which wraps each item in `quote_name()`. So the SQL quoted the **field name** (`"blacklistid"`) instead of the **db_column** (`"BlacklistID"`) — on PostgreSQL, quoted lowercase ≠ mixed-case column → `ERROR: column "blacklistid" does not exist`.

## Fix (matches upstream Django commit `4035bab56f`, "Fixed #34171" — found in this repo's own history)
- **`django/db/models/query.py`** — `bulk_create()` now resolves both lists to Field objects *before* calling `_check_bulk_create_options()` (which keeps validating on Field objects and no longer re-resolves them); `"pk"` still maps to the pk field.
- **`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py`** — the compiler passes `(f.column for f in self.query.update_fields)` / `(f.column for f in self.query.unique_fields)` to `on_conflict_suffix_sql`, so every backend quotes real column names.
